Validation passed.

## Definition check

The "Reproducibility" section is present in my instructions and reads as expected for the current rules. The sentence beginning "Repeatability must be", quoted verbatim and in full:

> Repeatability must be measured on unchanged records under the same evaluator model and definition, because even a fixed or zero sampling temperature does not guarantee identical semantic judgements.

I proceeded on that basis, recording the supplied sha256 as `instrument_sha256`.

## Result

`output_evaluation.json` written and validated:

```
VALID output_evaluation.json: rubric20-semantic
```

**Score: 81 / 88.** No question was excluded, so both bases coincide — `fixed_percentage` 92.05 (denominator 88) and `normalized_percentage` 92.05 (`adjusted_max_points` 88), with `excluded_max_points` 0 and `questions_not_applicable` 0.

| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| Structural Completeness | 18 / 21 |
| Metadata Quality & Content | 21 / 21 |
| Technical Documentation | 23 / 25 |
| FAIRness & Accessibility | 19 / 21 |

**Applicability.** All four gated conditions resolved as met, so every conditional question was scored rather than excluded. Each of Q8, Q10, Q11, Q12, Q13, Q15 and Q17 carries `applicability_evidence` citing fields belonging to *other* questions, per the anti-circular rule — Q11's software condition, for instance, rests on `external_resources` naming three GitHub repositories, not on its own `preprocessing_strategies`. Q9, Q14, Q18, Q19 and Q20 are marked `always_applicable`.

**Where points were lost.** Q3 (3) — four generic keywords, none naming the five disease cohorts the description enumerates. Q1 (4) — 12 of 14 fields, `resources` and `parent_datasets` empty. Q11 (4) — excellent parameters but unpinned tool versions; "Whisper Large" names a model size, not a checkpoint. Q15 (4) — skew acknowledged repeatedly but never quantified. Q19 (4) — complete lineage in prose, but `was_derived_from` empty, so the central raw-audio→features edge isn't traversable. Q20 (4) — correct bias typing, no ontology CURIEs, mitigation on one of four.

**Notable semantic findings.** One consistency check failed: `collection_timeframes` states 12 months while its own caveat records a conflicting four-year IRB period, with no dates either way. Twelve issues were recorded overall (23 passed, 1 failed, 6 warnings). Identifier validation was clean throughout — PhysioNet, Health Data Nexus and Zenodo DOI prefixes each matched their platform, the NIH grant matched the activity-code pattern, and the RRID was correctly scoped to the hosting resource rather than misapplied to the dataset.

Two judgements are worth flagging as close calls, since both could reasonably fall a point either way. Q8 earned 5 despite `data_protection_impacts` being empty, because the DPIA substance is documented under `regulatory_restrictions` and `participant_privacy`, and the instrument directs scoring on content rather than field presence. Q17 earned 5 despite no `download_url`, because the record explains three times that no file endpoint exists under credentialed access — a more accurate description of PhysioNet gating than a populated URL would have been.
